title: Gauge-fixed quantum signal-processing phase synthesis
difficulty_explanation: The solver must reconcile a precise SU(2) convention, a reflection gauge, complex parity-polynomial constraints, and a non-convex phase-factor inverse problem; polynomial fitting alone does not produce the required circuit artifact.
claim_boundary: No GPT-5.6-sol trial has been run; difficulty remains a hypothesis.

seed_protocol.base_seed_mapping: A verifier base seed b expands to the ordered three-instance schedule (b, b + 12, b + 28). An explicit --seeds list overrides that schedule.
seed_protocol.determinism_scope: The seed schedule mapping is runtime-independent, but exact generated public config bytes are identified by the evaluator-emitted case_digest under the pinned runtime.
seed_protocol.case_identity: SHA-256 of canonical JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, and full finite numeric values over the ordered exact public configs; functional stdout emits the full case_digest and protocol_seed in one structured orbit_q_case_identity JSON line.
seed_protocol.pinned_numpy_note: The target image pins NumPy 2.2.6; a seed alone is not a cross-runtime case identity, so trial manifests must bind the image/runtime and case_digest.

tensorcircuit_central_path: TensorCircuit Circuit for every QSP sequence evaluation
independent_oracle: NumPy complex 2x2 products plus Chebyshev and QSP identities; no TensorCircuit import
hardcoding_resistance: three generated targets from each verifier-only base seed
api_risks: Circuit.any(unitary=...) is required and was canaried only against tensorcircuit-nightly 1.7.0.dev20260618.
The expert assumes TensorCircuit RZ(theta)=exp(-i theta Z/2); the evaluator convention therefore uses theta=-2*phi.
complex64 JAX differentiation can stall near machine precision; evaluator thresholds intentionally remain above 1e-4.
